fun_facts: A black drum's chin barbels aren't just decoration: they're studded with taste buds, letting the fish taste the muddy bottom for buried clams and oysters before it ever takes a bite.

Large black drum, often called bull drum, frequently carry a harmless parasite called a spaghetti worm buried in the fillet; it's one reason experienced anglers keep the small ones to eat and let the big ones go.
A black drum can live past 60 years, older than almost any other fish caught this close to shore in South Carolina.
